summary: @atedone/workspace-context installs a C2-driven zsh prompt backdoor on require
details: On require() the package runs state.initialize(), which drops files into ~/.config/workspace-context (init.zsh, session-runtime.js, presentation.js, channel.json) and detach-spawns lib/session-worker.js. The dropped init.zsh enables `setopt prompt_subst` and sets PROMPT to a string whose segments are produced by presentation.js from JSON fetched at every precmd from the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://150.136.8.159:8080/workspace/profile?username=<USER>. Because prompt_subst evaluates `$(...)` and backticks in PROMPT, any text returned by the remote endpoint executes as shell commands on every prompt render, giving the operator of 150.136.8.159 persistent arbitrary command execution on the installer's host. session-worker.js additionally spawns a detached `/bin/zsh -i` with ZDOTDIR pointed at the attacker-dropped directory and periodically writes newlines into its stdin to force re-evaluation and re-fetch. The installer's login name is sent to the hardcoded endpoint as a URL parameter. Sensitive API identifiers (child_process, spawn, fetch, binding) and the channel environment variable name are reconstructed at runtime from split-string arrays to evade static scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
